csm_source_note: ESPIRiT csm — the SAME file configs/g0_fullsample.yaml's csm_path points at; deliberately NOT load_trainer_mat's embedded `map` field (verified 111% relative Frobenius difference between the two, see module docstring)
achieved_npts_note: max_primitives above is only the CLI cap; this is the actual point count the cold-start Gaussian arm ran with (adaptive_control disabled, fixed for the whole run — see results_crisp/g0_full_train_meta.json). Without this field the primitive-count half of the <=1e6-at-<=2x gate cannot be verified from this file alone.
regularizer_deviation_caveat: The Gaussian arm trained with the shipped winner config's regularisers (tv_weight 0.06, kspace_freq_adaptive true, kspace_center_weight 0.3, kspace_high_weight 2.2 -- see configs/g0_fullsample.yaml), not the plan's Task 8 Step 4 settings (--lambda_geo 0.0 --kspace_high 1.0). Never amended against the written plan. Direction is conservative: those regularisers were tuned for undersampled reconstruction, not this full-sampling capacity probe, so they if anything handicap this arm -- a handicapped arm still passed. Read ratio_gaussian_over_reference as a LOWER BOUND on the representation's capability, not its ceiling.
cross_experiment_csm_warning: G2 (results_crisp/g2_voxel_huangyuwei.json) loads CSM via crisp.io.load_trainer_mat (the trainer .mat's embedded `map` field), a DIFFERENT array from the ESPIRiT csm this file uses -- 111% relative Frobenius difference (see csm_source_note above). G2's E_unobs and this file's E_coil_full are therefore computed under different forward operators A=FS and are not on a common scale; do not compute a 'gap to the ceiling' by comparing them.
comparison_handicap: complex-vs-complex: Gaussian arm is the raw JointTrainer._render() output (real image-domain amplitude+phase, no DC substitution, no magnitude cast); reference arm is the full complex CG-SENSE solution. Neither side has had phase stripped.
